verdict.rationale: The GitHub sync docs say you can write code "in Base44" and keep it in sync with local development, which implies some in-builder code editing. This is a single passing mention inside the GitHub integration page, and there are no dedicated docs for an in-editor code view. Other evidence covers AI-driven code changes, ejecting code, or external agents, which are not direct editing inside the builder. missing for 10: dedicated documentation of an in-builder code viewer/editor, details on which files (frontend/backend) can be opened and edited, any hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can open and edit the generated source code directly inside the builder

citations.quote: Connect your app to GitHub to write code in your local development environment or in Base44 and keep them in sync with each other.
